title: Choose the visual world for Vizball
question: Colors (pitch green, gold, red) and the Fester font are fixed either way. Keep the rolled direction, take my pick, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Toghu Stitch
options.lineage: Cameroonian Toghu ceremonial embroidery from the Grassfields
options.thesis: Vizball worn like a ceremonial garment: every section is a stitched band on deep velvet green.
options.viewport: Giant Fester Heavy VIZBALL over a full-bleed match photo, framed by a gold/red/green diamond band that embroiders itself in on load; the field diagram is chain-stitched in gold beside the primary action.
options.risk: Can read as ethnic ornament if the bands stop doing structural work; Toghu is Grassfields regalia, so motifs stay generic geometry.

raised.raise: The sport's real facts (48 × 24, 12 balls, 4 vs 5, 3/2/1 points, 2007) set as a fixed-digit bank that rolls into place.
The 4 vs 5 asymmetry shown as two hard halves that swap sides, as the teams do after each period.
Every element labelled with the rulebook's own codes (CC, GC, Z3, PC, B), like numbered pattern pieces.

options.label: Le Terrain
options.lineage: Vizball's official 48 × 24 m field diagram and referee chalk lines
options.thesis: The page is the pitch: the official field's chalk lines draw themselves as you scroll and each section is a zone of play.
options.viewport: Full-screen pitch-green field: the great circle, peripheral circles and Z3/Z2/Z1 zones draw in chalk around a giant VIZBALL; a ball traces the play loop; a 'Prochain match' widget and the 'Découvrir le sport' action sit on the touchline.
options.risk: Closest to the Lando Norris Site-of-the-Year pattern (line motif, dark ground, one hot accent), which is where many premium sport sites now land.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Every fact arrives as a glowing digit in a glass tube.
options.case: Fuses poorly: players and sponsors don't recognise lab instruments in a sport.
options.kept: Quantities as interface: fixed digit positions for the sport's real numbers.
options.risk: Reads as a gadget, not a sport.

options.label: Mixtape J-card
options.thesis: The site as a mixtape: side A, side B.
options.viewport: A folded J-card with the rules as a tracklist.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link to the sport or its audience.
options.kept: Two hard halves with a physical flip, matching the 4 vs 5 role swap.

options.label: Sewing Pattern
options.thesis: The field as a cutting layout of numbered pieces.
options.viewport: Tissue sheet with the zones as dashed pieces.
options.case: Fuses poorly: audience doesn't identify; clarity suffers.
options.kept: Rigorous labelling: every zone carries its official code.

options.label: Stitched Sampler
options.thesis: Learning the sport band by band, simplest first.
options.viewport: Bands of rules stitched in increasing difficulty.
options.case: Fuses poorly: European domestic craft, not Cameroonian sport.
options.kept: Pages descend in learning order, simplest rule first.

options.label: Rain-night City
options.thesis: The city's lights as a living timeline.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link to the sport's mechanism.
options.kept: Time-indexed states: the page shifts like a match through its 4 periods.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.thesis: Windows and icons as the sport's interface.
options.case: Fuses poorly: conflicts with the fixed palette and audience.
options.kept: Every state visibly distinct, pressed, selected, disabled.

canonCard.label: The federation standard
canonCard.thesis: What sport federation sites ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Full-bleed photo carousel hero, a stat bar, news cards, a CTA band.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other federation site by design.
